newsitem.title: FRANCE: KLM to raise ex-Paris cargo rates March 1.
newsitem.headline: KLM to raise ex-Paris cargo rates March 1.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said it planned to increase its ex-Paris cargo rates on selected destinations by between five and 10 percent, effective March 1.
KLM last increased its ex-Paris cargo rates in October 1996.

"The increases centre largely on Far East routes where market demand is strongest and also India, where rates have traditionally been very low," KLM director of sales, southern Europe, Marcel Blomjous, told Reuters.
There would also be increases in KLM's ex-Paris rates to the U.S but on a smaller-scale to those for the Far East and India, Blomjous said.

"Main-deck capacity aside, there is only limited scope to increase rates significantly on U.S. routes given the number of belly-carriers on Transatlantic routes who do not hesitate to dump on rates," he stated.
The rates increases were put into perspective when one considered that cargo yields have been falling steadily year-on-year, over the past decade, Blomjous added.
"Airlines need to invest long-term in the air cargo sector to ensure greater demands on quality of service from customers. However, they can only do this if a certain level of revenues is generated."
Blomjous added he was "moderately optimistic" on the market outlook for 1997 even though it was unlikely there would be the kind of growth achieved in 1995.

"One factor is the strengthening of the dollar which should provide a boost to European exports. However, it could also have a negative aspect for a carrier like KLM which has an important focus on import traffic. We'll just have to wait and see." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
